options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms by a set date, once consideration is paid
options.b: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration
options.c: A right of first refusal to match any third-party offer the owner later accepts
options.d: Equitable title to the property from signing, as under an installment land contract

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses an option with a bilateral purchase contract; the optionee may buy but is not obligated to.
distractorExplanations.c: A right of first refusal depends on a third-party offer; an option lets the optionee buy on fixed terms at will.
distractorExplanations.d: Equitable title arises under a contract for deed or sales contract; an optionee holds only a contract right.

options.a: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.b: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.c: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.a: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.b: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: Proceed as a dual agent after giving the buyer written notice of the relationship
options.b: Switch to representing the buyer while keeping the seller's listing active for both
options.c: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.d: Terminate the listing agreement unilaterally and refund the seller's marketing costs

distractorExplanations.a: Dual agency requires informed consent from both parties; notice to the buyer alone cannot replace the seller's consent.
distractorExplanations.b: Representing the buyer while still holding the listing is undisclosed dual agency, the exact thing the seller refused.
distractorExplanations.d: Refusing dual agency does not let the broker abandon the listing; the broker simply declines to represent the buyer.

options.a: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.b: Using client trust money for the broker's own business or personal expenses
options.c: Depositing several clients' earnest money deposits into one trust account
options.d: Holding earnest money beyond the deadline for depositing it into escrow

distractorExplanations.b: Spending trust money on the broker's own expenses is conversion, a separate and more serious violation.
distractorExplanations.c: Pooling multiple clients' funds in one properly kept trust account is permitted; mixing in broker money is not.
distractorExplanations.d: Late deposit is a timeliness violation of trust-account rules, not the mixing of trust and personal funds.

options.a: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.b: Parties may still perform within a reasonable time after each stated deadline passes
options.c: The closing date is firm, but other contingency deadlines may slip
options.d: The offer expires if the seller does not accept it within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.b: That is the default rule when the clause is absent; time is of the essence makes the stated deadlines strictly enforceable.
distractorExplanations.c: The clause applies to all contract dates, including inspection, financing, and appraisal contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the clause with an offer's expiration term; time is of the essence governs performance deadlines in the contract.

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term
options.d: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.c: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: At closing, when the broker's compensation appears on the Closing Disclosure
options.b: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises
options.c: Only after an offer is accepted and both parties have signed the contract
options.d: After the inspection period ends, once the buyer is committed to the purchase

distractorExplanations.a: Closing is far too late; informed consent to dual or designated agency must come before the parties rely on it.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting until after acceptance denies the parties informed consent during negotiations, when the conflict matters most.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure tied to a later contract milestone is too late; it is required when the dual relationship first arises.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated, per applicable rules.

options.a: The listing broker earns a commission during the term except when the seller personally finds the buyer
options.b: Any cooperating broker who is the procuring cause earns the commission, and the seller may list with other firms
options.c: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.d: The broker keeps any proceeds above the seller's stated net price as compensation for the sale

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and the seller may list with several firms.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, which is restricted or banned in many places; it is a compensation method, not exclusive right-to-sell.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term (per the agreement).

options.a: The seller's reason for selling and lowest acceptable price, even if the seller objects
options.b: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood, since it may affect desirability
options.c: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.d: Obvious patent defects, while hidden latent defects are left for the buyer's own inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts a buyer must be told.
distractorExplanations.b: Commenting on a neighborhood's race or religion is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required material-fact disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: known latent (hidden) defects are exactly what must be disclosed, because a buyer cannot readily discover them.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared, as required by law; confidential motivations may be protected.

options.a: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.b: A false statement of a material fact that the licensee knew to be untrue
options.c: An unintentional misstatement of a measurable fact, such as the home's square footage
options.d: An ad that omits the brokerage name and lists only a phone number (a blind ad)

distractorExplanations.b: A knowing false statement of material fact is intentional misrepresentation (fraud), not puffing, which is mere opinion.
distractorExplanations.c: Misstating a measurable fact is negligent misrepresentation; puffing involves subjective opinion such as 'stunning view'.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses puffing with a blind ad, which is an advertising violation for failing to identify the brokerage.

options.a: Practicing law any time they fill in a standard form's blanks for a client
options.b: Permitted to draft custom clauses as long as the client signs a waiver
options.c: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.d: Required to have the client's attorney approve each filled-in form first

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in approved standard forms is generally permitted for licensees; drafting new legal language is what crosses into law practice.
distractorExplanations.b: A client waiver does not authorize a licensee to practice law; drafting novel legal clauses remains unauthorized practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Attorney review may be advisable or a contract contingency, but it is not a general prerequisite to completing standard forms.

options.a: Must acquire title at the same time and by the same deed as each other
options.b: Hold equal undivided shares, and a deceased owner's share passes to the others
options.c: Cannot sell or will their share without the other co-owners' consent
options.d: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified

distractorExplanations.a: Unity of time and title are joint tenancy requirements; tenants in common may acquire their shares at different times by different deeds.
distractorExplanations.b: Equal shares plus right of survivorship are joint tenancy features; a tenant in common's share passes to heirs or devisees.
distractorExplanations.c: A tenant in common may freely sell, mortgage, or will an undivided share without the other co-owners' consent.

options.a: Interest alone, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.b: Part of the interest, with the unpaid rest added to the balance
options.c: Interest plus escrowed taxes and insurance, with no principal reduction
options.d: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an interest-only or balloon loan; an amortizing payment repays principal with each installment.
distractorExplanations.b: Adding unpaid interest to the balance is negative amortization, the opposite of a fully amortizing payment.
distractorExplanations.c: Escrowed taxes and insurance may be added to PITI, but an amortizing payment still reduces principal every month.

options.a: Requiring APR and finance charge disclosures for all consumer credit
options.b: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.c: Requiring lenders to report loan data by census tract to regulators
options.d: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures

distractorExplanations.a: APR and finance-charge disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA's settlement-services focus.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA); RESPA targets settlement kickbacks and closing-cost disclosure.
distractorExplanations.c: Census-tract loan reporting is the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act (HMDA), which tracks lending patterns, not settlement costs.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures in covered transactions (with TRID integration for many loans).

options.a: Maximum loan-to-value ratios that lenders may offer on certain loans
options.b: Minimum disclosures of APR and finance charges on consumer loans
options.c: Maximum property tax rates that local governments may levy
options.d: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans

distractorExplanations.a: LTV limits come from lender and investor underwriting guidelines, not usury laws, which cap the interest rate charged.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), which requires cost disclosure but does not cap interest rates.
distractorExplanations.c: Property tax limits are set by tax and levy laws; usury laws apply to interest charged by lenders on loans.

options.a: Give the buyer a pricing opinion as long as the seller is not told about it
options.b: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can make a fair offer
options.c: Refuse to give the buyer any property facts until the buyer signs an offer
options.d: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role

distractorExplanations.a: Advising the buyer on price behind the seller's back breaches the listing agent's loyalty duty to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.b: Disclosing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality owed to the seller; fair treatment of a customer does not require it.
distractorExplanations.c: Customers are still owed honest disclosure of material facts; limited service to a customer does not mean withholding facts.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. If the buyer wants advocacy, buyer agency (or disclosed dual agency where allowed) must be properly created first.

options.a: Was induced by fraud or was a minor
options.b: Did not record the signed contract
options.c: Signed under a mistake about market value
options.d: Later found a better deal elsewhere

distractorExplanations.b: Recording gives notice to third parties; an unrecorded contract is still valid and enforceable between the parties.
distractorExplanations.c: A party's own misjudgment of value is not a ground to avoid a contract; fraud or lack of capacity is.
distractorExplanations.d: Buyer's remorse or a better alternative is not a legal ground to avoid a binding contract.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the contract is voidable depends on the circumstances, and only the protected party may void it.

options.a: The broker's compensation is a flat fee set by the state commission
options.b: The seller owes the broker a commission even if no buyer is ever found
options.c: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.d: The listing broker cannot cooperate with or share fees with buyer brokers

distractorExplanations.a: Commissions are negotiable and no state commission sets a flat fee; a net listing pays the open-ended excess over the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.b: Owing a fee without a sale is not a net-listing feature; a net listing pays the broker the excess over the net price at sale.
distractorExplanations.d: Net listings do not bar cooperation with buyer brokers; the concern is the broker's incentive to underprice.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings can incentivize underpricing relative to the seller's interests and are banned or tightly regulated in many places. That open-ended spread creates a conflict of interest, since the broker gains by steering the seller to a low net figure.

options.a: Curtesy
options.b: Homestead
options.c: Survivorship
options.d: Inheritance by heirs

distractorExplanations.a: Curtesy is a husband's historical interest in a deceased wife's estate, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.b: Homestead protects a residence from certain creditors; it is not the defining feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.d: Passing a co-owner's share to heirs is what survivorship prevents; that describes tenancy in common.

options.a: Public use and the owner's written consent to sell
options.b: Compensation equal to the property's assessed tax value
options.c: Public use/purpose and just compensation
options.d: A blight finding by the court

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; the owner's consent is not required, only public use and just compensation.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation is generally fair market value, not the assessor's value used for property taxes.
distractorExplanations.d: Blight findings relate to redevelopment programs; the constitutional test is public use plus just compensation.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public purpose and just compensation under the Constitution. This is the Fifth Amendment takings framework, applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment.

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: When the life tenant sells the property
options.c: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.d: When the life tenant moves out of the home

distractorExplanations.a: The remainderman's death does not end the estate; the remainder passes to the remainderman's estate and the measuring life still controls.
distractorExplanations.b: A life tenant can convey the interest, but the buyer holds it only until the measuring life dies (estate pur autre vie).
distractorExplanations.d: Vacating the property does not terminate a life estate; the end of the measuring life (or other defined event) does.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; remainder/reversion follows. The deed or will may also define other terminating events.

options.a: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability
options.b: A zoning variance granted to the current owner
options.c: A lender's commitment letter issued before closing
options.d: A quiet title judgment that removes a disputed claim to ownership

distractorExplanations.b: A variance is land-use relief from the zoning authority, not a claim against ownership of the parcel.
distractorExplanations.c: A loan commitment is financing paperwork between lender and borrower; it creates no adverse claim against title.
distractorExplanations.d: A quiet title action is the cure for a cloud; the judgment removes the doubt rather than creating it.

options.a: Rezoning of an entire district by amending the zoning map
options.b: Continuation of a use that predates the current zoning law
options.c: Approval of a conditional use the ordinance already allows by permit
options.d: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship

distractorExplanations.a: Changing the map for a whole district is a rezoning (zoning amendment), not a variance for one parcel.
distractorExplanations.b: A use that existed before the ordinance is a nonconforming (grandfathered) use, not a variance.
distractorExplanations.c: A conditional or special-use permit allows a use the code already contemplates; a variance grants hardship relief from a requirement.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. Variances are granted by the zoning authority, usually a zoning board of appeals.

options.a: Delivering the deed to the grantee at closing
options.b: Notarizing the deed before a licensed notary
options.c: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.d: Filing the deed with the local tax assessor

distractorExplanations.a: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties but do not give notice to the rest of the world.
distractorExplanations.b: Acknowledgment makes a deed eligible for recording; by itself it does not give constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Assessor records are kept for taxation; constructive notice comes from the recorder's public land records.

options.a: Land bordering a still lake or an ocean shoreline
options.b: Groundwater pumped from a well under the parcel
options.c: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.d: Water rights earned by first beneficial use in time

distractorExplanations.a: Lakes and oceans involve littoral rights; riparian rights concern land along flowing water.
distractorExplanations.b: Percolating groundwater is governed by separate groundwater doctrines, not riparian rights.
distractorExplanations.d: First-in-time beneficial use is the prior appropriation doctrine, the western alternative to riparian rights.

options.a: 1% of the purchase price
options.b: 1% of the down payment
options.c: A 1% cut in the interest rate
options.d: 1% of the loan amount

distractorExplanations.a: Points are computed on the loan amount, not the price; with a down payment the two figures differ.
distractorExplanations.b: The down payment is not the base for points; one point equals 1% of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses the cost of a point with its effect; one point typically buys down the rate by a fraction of a percent.

options.a: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays late
options.b: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early
options.c: Lets the lender call the loan if the property is sold
options.d: Protects the borrower from rate increases after closing

distractorExplanations.a: A charge for paying late is a late fee under the note; a prepayment penalty applies to paying off early.
distractorExplanations.c: Calling the loan on transfer of the property is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, not a prepayment penalty.
distractorExplanations.d: Protection from rate changes is a rate lock or fixed-rate feature, unrelated to charges for early payoff.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. It applies only when the note allows it and the law permits it.

options.a: Is reset by the borrower's credit score at each adjustment
options.b: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
options.c: Can adjust based on the index alone, with no rate caps
options.d: Stays fixed for the loan term unless the borrower refinances

distractorExplanations.a: Credit affects the margin offered at origination; later adjustments follow the index while the margin stays fixed.
distractorExplanations.c: ARMs add a fixed margin to the index and usually carry periodic and lifetime caps.
distractorExplanations.d: A rate fixed for the full term describes a fixed-rate mortgage, not an adjustable-rate mortgage.

options.a: Physical defects found by the buyer's home inspector
options.b: Fire, flood, and wind damage to the structure
options.c: Borrower default on the mortgage note after closing
options.d: Covered title defects and claims against ownership

distractorExplanations.a: Physical condition issues are inspection or home-warranty matters; title insurance covers ownership defects.
distractorExplanations.b: Casualty losses are covered by hazard (homeowner's) and flood insurance, not by title insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: Default risk is covered by mortgage insurance (PMI or FHA MIP), not by an owner's or lender's title policy.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Owner's/lender's title policies insure against covered title risks, not casualty. Coverage follows the policy terms, schedule of exceptions and exclusions.

options.a: The buyer is credited; it reduces cash needed
options.b: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed
options.c: The seller is charged; it reduces the seller's proceeds
options.d: The lender pays the item outside of closing

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a credit to the buyer; a debit is a charge that increases the buyer's cash due at closing.
distractorExplanations.c: A debit to the buyer charges the buyer, not the seller; seller debits appear in the seller's column.
distractorExplanations.d: Items paid outside closing (POC) are noted separately; a buyer debit is charged to the buyer at settlement.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For the seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

options.a: Originate purchase loans directly to homebuyers
options.b: Insure lenders against default on low-down loans
options.c: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity
options.d: Set the federal funds rate that drives mortgage pricing

distractorExplanations.a: Originating loans to consumers is the primary mortgage market, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.b: Default insurance is provided by FHA or private mortgage insurers, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.d: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target; the secondary market buys and sells existing loans.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Entities like Fannie/Freddie (and others) provide liquidity by purchasing loans. Selling loans frees originators' capital so they can lend again.

options.a: Fund construction draws as a builder completes each stage of a new custom home
options.b: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.c: Let a seller finance the buyer's purchase by carrying back a second mortgage note
options.d: Combine a first mortgage with a second loan so the buyer avoids private mortgage insurance

distractorExplanations.a: Staged draws released as building progresses describe a construction loan, not a bridge loan.
distractorExplanations.c: A seller carryback is purchase-money seller financing, not short-term gap financing between two homes.
distractorExplanations.d: A first plus a second loan to avoid PMI is a piggyback (80-10-10) structure, not a bridge loan.

options.a: Substitutes for the license law where firm policy and the statute conflict
options.b: Shifts liability for an agent's misconduct from the broker to the agent
options.c: Sets commission rates that cooperating brokerages in the area must accept
options.d: Documents supervision standards and compliant procedures for affiliated licensees

distractorExplanations.a: Firm policy cannot override statute or commission rules; where they conflict, the law controls.
distractorExplanations.b: A manual supports supervision but does not relieve the supervising broker of responsibility for affiliated licensees.
distractorExplanations.c: Commissions are negotiable; a firm cannot fix rates for other brokerages, which would also raise antitrust issues.

options.a: Pay the rebate from the buyer's escrow deposit before closing without lender notice
options.b: Decline because federal RESPA bans all commission rebates to buyers
options.c: Pay the rebate privately after closing so it stays off the settlement statement
options.d: Follow brokerage rules on rebates and ensure any payment is lawful and disclosed

distractorExplanations.a: Rebates come from the broker's commission and are disclosed to the lender; tapping escrow funds and hiding it is improper.
distractorExplanations.b: RESPA does not ban a disclosed commission rebate to a buyer; legality turns on state law and lender rules.
distractorExplanations.c: Hiding a rebate from the settlement statement and lender can amount to mortgage fraud; it must be disclosed.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-ma-licens.explanation: Rebate legality varies; compliance and disclosure are essential. Where permitted, rebates must also satisfy any rules set by the state licensing authority.

options.a: Negotiate offers for the associate while licensed with a different brokerage
options.b: Be paid commission directly by the associate instead of through the broker
options.c: Perform licensed activities only within their own license authority
options.d: Sign listing agreements in the associate's name

distractorExplanations.a: A licensee may act only for the brokerage holding their license; working another firm's deals violates affiliation rules.
distractorExplanations.b: Compensation for licensed activity must flow through the employing broker, not directly from another agent.
distractorExplanations.d: Listings are brokerage contracts; an assistant cannot sign as, or for, another licensee without authority.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-ma-licens.explanation: Licensed assistants still must stay within license and supervision rules. They must also follow brokerage affiliation and supervision rules.

options.a: Protect confidential client information and not disclose without authority
options.b: Disclose it, because the fiduciary duties owed to the seller ended at closing
options.c: Disclose it, because the buyer was a party to the same transaction
options.d: Ask the closing attorney to release it from the settlement file

distractorExplanations.b: Confidentiality about a client's personal information survives closing, unlike most other agency duties.
distractorExplanations.c: Being the other party to the deal gives the buyer no right to the seller's confidential personal information.
distractorExplanations.d: Routing the request through the settlement agent still discloses confidential information without the seller's authority.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-ma-licens.explanation: Confidentiality can survive closing for non-public personal information. Disclosure is appropriate only with the seller's authority or a legal requirement such as a subpoena.

options.a: Deposited into the brokerage operating account until the contract closes
options.b: Held uncashed in the transaction file until closing to avoid any refund disputes
options.c: Deposited into the listing agent's own escrow account for that client
options.d: Deposited into a properly designated trust/escrow account within required timelines

distractorExplanations.a: Placing client funds in the operating account is commingling, even if the broker tracks them separately.
distractorExplanations.b: Funds must be deposited within the required time; holding the check until closing breaks that timeline.
distractorExplanations.c: Trust accounts are maintained by the broker or firm; individual associates do not hold their own escrow accounts.

options.a: Keep the license with the old broker until every pending deal there closes
options.b: Apply for a new license and retake the state portion of the exam
options.c: Follow transfer procedures so the license is properly affiliated
options.d: Wait until the license renewal date to report the new broker

distractorExplanations.a: A licensee may be affiliated with one broker at a time; the license transfers now while pending deals stay with the old firm.
distractorExplanations.b: Changing brokers is a transfer of an existing license, not a new application or re-examination.
distractorExplanations.d: Transfers must be reported when the move happens, not deferred to the next renewal cycle.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-ma-licens.explanation: Affiliation changes require regulatory notice/transfer steps. This usually includes notifying the state licensing authority of the new affiliation.

options.a: Keeping records until the buyer's loan is paid off
options.b: Keeping trust records but discarding listing and sales files
options.c: Letting the title company keep the records instead of the firm
options.d: Keeping transaction records for the required period

distractorExplanations.a: Retention runs for a set period after the transaction, not for the life of a 30-year mortgage.
distractorExplanations.b: Retention covers contracts, agency disclosures and transaction files, not just trust account records.
distractorExplanations.c: The broker must maintain and produce its own records; a settlement agent's file does not satisfy the broker's duty.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-ma-licens.explanation: Statutory retention periods protect consumers and enable audits. The retention period is set by the state licensing authority's rules.

options.a: Acceptable if the licensee states it in writing in the offer
options.b: Acceptable puffing because future value is an opinion
options.c: Generally improper/misleading and can be a license law violation
options.d: Allowed when the brokerage carries errors and omissions insurance

distractorExplanations.a: Putting a guaranteed profit in writing does not cure the misrepresentation; it simply documents it.
distractorExplanations.b: Puffing is vague praise; a direct promise of a specific future profit is a misrepresentation, not puffing.
distractorExplanations.d: E&O coverage does not make a deceptive guarantee lawful and often excludes intentional misrepresentation.

options.a: After the listing agent screens out the weaker offers
options.b: At the next scheduled weekly seller update
options.c: Once the buyer's lender issues a loan approval
options.d: Promptly as required by agency and license rules

distractorExplanations.a: Offers go to the seller promptly unless the seller gave lawful written instructions; agents do not filter them.
distractorExplanations.b: Waiting for a routine weekly update delays presentation; offers must be presented promptly.
distractorExplanations.c: Offers are presented when received; financing approval is a later contingency, not a precondition for presentation.

options.a: Moves with the associate, who becomes responsible for those records
options.b: Remains with the brokerage; the firm retains responsibility for records
options.c: Is split so the associate keeps open deals and the firm keeps closed ones
options.d: Goes to the state commission for storage until the files expire

distractorExplanations.a: Transaction files belong to the brokerage; a departing associate cannot take control of them.
distractorExplanations.c: Pending transactions are brokerage contracts; they do not move with the associate without the broker's agreement.
distractorExplanations.d: The licensing authority does not store brokerage files; the firm retains them for the required period.

options.a: They help detect shortages/overages and demonstrate compliance
options.b: They let the broker take earned interest as operating income
options.c: They replace the need for separate ledgers for each transaction
options.d: They are needed only when the account is audited by the commission

distractorExplanations.b: Reconciliation does not authorize moving trust interest to operating funds; interest handling is set by law and agreement.
distractorExplanations.c: Reconciliation compares the bank statement, the journal and each client ledger; it does not replace the ledgers.
distractorExplanations.d: Reconciliation is a routine periodic duty (commonly monthly), not something done only when an audit occurs.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-ma-licens.explanation: Regular reconciliation is a core trust-account control. Reconciled records are what the licensing authority reviews in a trust account audit.

options.a: Contact the complainant to negotiate withdrawal of the complaint
options.b: Decline to answer until the complainant files a civil lawsuit
options.c: Cooperate as required and respond truthfully within deadlines
options.d: Let the supervising broker answer on the associate's behalf

distractorExplanations.a: Pressuring a complainant to withdraw can be treated as interference, and the Board may proceed even if it is withdrawn.
distractorExplanations.b: The Board's disciplinary process is separate from civil litigation; the licensee must respond within the Board's deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: The licensee named in the complaint must respond personally; a broker's response does not substitute for it.

options.a: Illegal under federal fair housing law and typically also violates license standards
options.b: Legal if the seller gives the instruction in writing and the agent documents it
options.c: Illegal under state law but exempt from the federal Fair Housing Act for brokers
options.d: Legal for owner-occupied single-family homes when a licensee lists the property

distractorExplanations.b: A seller's written instruction does not make discrimination lawful; the agent must refuse to follow it.
distractorExplanations.c: Brokered sales are covered by the federal Fair Housing Act; licensees get no exemption from it.
distractorExplanations.d: The single-family owner exemption is lost when the owner uses a real estate licensee to sell or rent.

ma-real-estate-readiness-check-ma-licens.explanation: Fair housing prohibitions override discriminatory seller instructions. State license law and state anti-discrimination law add their own penalties.
